overview.headline: Master Ethical Email Campaigns, Lifecycle Automations & Sender Deliverability.
overview.summary: A practical 5-week, 40-hour certification course designed to teach permission-based email marketing from subscriber acquisition to automated lifecycle journeys and performance measurement. Learners gain hands-on proficiency using Mailchimp or Brevo, master sender authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) compliant with Google's sender guidelines, design conversion-focused responsive email campaigns, construct automated welcome and nurture workflows, and analyze real campaign metrics in Google Sheets. Students graduate with a professional portfolio containing a segmented database, 3 polished email campaigns, 2 automated journeys, and an executive campaign performance report.

why_now.market_need: Email remains the highest-ROI owned digital marketing channel. As third-party cookies decline and ad costs rise, businesses prioritize owned subscriber relationships and automated lifecycle retention.
why_now.deliverability_shift: Major mailbox providers (Google, Yahoo) now enforce strict sender authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and low spam complaint thresholds (<0.1%), making professional deliverability expertise essential.
why_now.career_relevance: Companies need email marketing specialists who understand lifecycle automation, segmentation, and compliance rather than casual newsletter blast senders.

learning_outcomes: Develop an ethical email marketing strategy and organize a permission-based subscriber database with clean segmentation.
Audit sending domains for SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment, ensuring compliance with Google sender guidelines and RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe.
Design 3 responsive, brand-aligned email campaigns (Welcome, Educational/Nurture, Promotional) with high-converting copy and CTAs.
Build 2 visual lifecycle automation workflows (Welcome/Onboarding and Lead Nurture/Reactivation) using conditional branching in Mailchimp or Brevo.
Apply lightweight CRM concepts to manage contact lifecycle stages and connect subscriber engagement with sales outcomes.
Execute email A/B testing on subject lines, preview text, and send times while interpreting statistical significance.
Analyze campaign analytics (Deliverability, Clicks, Conversions, Unsubscribes) while understanding modern open-tracking limitations (Apple MPP).
Produce an executive email marketing performance dashboard in Google Sheets with data-backed optimization recommendations.

faq.question: What is the Email Marketing & Automation course?
faq.answer: The Email Marketing & Automation course is a practical 5-week, 40-hour certification program that teaches permission-based email marketing, modern sender authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), responsive campaign design, automated customer journeys, and performance measurement. It focuses on turning subscribers into loyal customers through ethical, high-converting lifecycle communication.

faq.question: Is this course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes, the course is designed for beginners to intermediate learners. It starts with email marketing fundamentals, permission management, and basic segmentation before advancing to deliverability audits, responsive visual layout design, automated trigger workflows, and campaign analytics. No prior coding or technical marketing background is required.

faq.question: What are the course fees and duration?
faq.answer: The course duration is 5 Weeks comprising 40 guided instructional hours across 5 comprehensive modules. The transparent institutional fee is ₹5,900 plus applicable taxes under our Truth in Pricing policy, with zero hidden charges or fake countdown discounts.

faq.question: Will I learn Mailchimp or Brevo?
faq.answer: You will receive hands-on practical training using either Mailchimp or Brevo as the primary teaching platform, with one platform selected for each cohort based on curriculum objectives and feature availability. Both platforms provide excellent visual drag-and-drop editors, contact management, and automation workflow builders.

faq.question: Does the course cover email automation?
faq.answer: Yes, email automation is a major pillar of the course. Module 04 is dedicated to building multi-step automated journeys, including welcome onboarding sequences, lead-nurturing workflows, reactivation triggers, time delays, and conditional if/else branching.

faq.question: Will I learn SPF, DKIM and DMARC?
faq.answer: Yes, Module 02 provides dedicated practical training on email authentication protocols: Sender Policy Framework (SPF), DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM), and Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting & Conformance (DMARC), ensuring compliance with current Google and Yahoo sender guidelines.

faq.question: What is email deliverability?
faq.answer: Email deliverability refers to whether your sent emails successfully reach subscribers' primary inboxes rather than being rejected or routed to the spam folder. You will learn to audit sending domains, monitor spam complaint rates (keeping them under 0.1%), manage bounces, and maintain sender reputation.

faq.question: Will I learn subscriber segmentation?
faq.answer: Yes, you will learn how to organize subscribers using demographic, interest-based, and behavioral/lifecycle criteria (such as new leads, active customers, or inactive contacts) to send targeted, highly relevant messages that generate higher engagement.

faq.question: Can I build automated welcome and nurture sequences?
faq.answer: Yes, in Portfolio Project 03, you will build and document two complete automation journeys: a 4-part welcome onboarding workflow and a behavior-based lead nurture or reactivation sequence with clear delay and exit rules.

faq.question: Does the course teach HubSpot CRM?
faq.answer: The course covers foundational lightweight CRM concepts using HubSpot CRM, teaching how to track contact lifecycle stages (Subscriber, Lead, MQL, Customer) and understand data flows between CRM contact records and email marketing automation.

faq.question: Are practical portfolio projects included?
faq.answer: Yes, you will complete 4 portfolio-ready deliverables: (1) a Permission-Based Subscriber Database with segmentation rules, (2) Three Responsive Email Campaigns (Welcome, Nurture, Promotional), (3) Two Automated Lifecycle Workflows, and (4) an Email Campaign Performance Report.

faq.question: Will I learn A/B testing and analytics?
faq.answer: Yes, Module 05 covers email campaign measurement, click-through rates, conversion tracking, Apple Mail Privacy Protection (MPP) open-tracking limitations, and conducting structured A/B tests on subject lines, preview text, and calls to action.

faq.question: Do I need a paid email marketing account?
faq.answer: No, all practical classroom exercises and portfolio projects are structured to work within the free tiers of Mailchimp or Brevo, or through controlled simulation environments. Paid third-party tool subscriptions are not required.

faq.question: Does the course require coding?
faq.answer: No, coding is not required. You will use modern visual drag-and-drop email builders and visual automation journey canvases in Mailchimp or Brevo. Basic HTML email concepts are explained conceptually for layout awareness, but no programming is necessary.

faq.question: What career opportunities can I pursue?
faq.answer: Graduates are equipped for practical roles such as Email Marketing Executive, Junior Email Marketing Specialist, Marketing Automation Assistant, Lifecycle Marketing Coordinator, CRM Marketing Assistant, or Email Campaign Coordinator, as well as providing freelance email marketing services to businesses.

modules.module_purpose: Master email deliverability mechanics, configure sender authentication protocols (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) in accordance with Google's sender guidelines, monitor domain reputation, and ensure RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe compliance.
mandatory_coverage: Email deliverability fundamentals: understanding the technical path from mail server to inbox

Email sender identity: friendly From name, From address, Reply-To address, and Return-Path headers

DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM): public/private key pairs, cryptographic header signatures, and tampering prevention
Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting & Conformance (DMARC): policy enforcement, alignment, and reporting
SPF alignment and DKIM alignment concepts: matching header domains with authentication domains
DMARC policies: p=none (monitoring), p=quarantine (spam folder), and p=reject (block outright)
DNS record fundamentals: configuring TXT and CNAME records with domain registrars
Domain reputation: how Google, Yahoo, and Microsoft track historical sender trust over time
IP reputation concepts: dedicated IP addresses versus shared IP pools in platforms like Mailchimp and Brevo
Sender health: key health indicators (low bounces, low spam complaints, high engagement)
Spam complaint rates: the critical importance of keeping spam complaints below 0.1% (and never exceeding 0.3%)
Hard bounces and soft bounces: permanent delivery failures (invalid address) versus temporary issues (mailbox full)
Invalid contact management: immediate removal of hard bounces to protect sender score
Suppression lists: automated suppression of bounced, unsubscribed, and spam-flagged contacts
Unsubscribe processes: making unsubscribing effortless to prevent users from hitting the spam button
One-click unsubscribe requirements: understanding RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe header specifications
RFC 8058 awareness: mandatory headers for bulk marketing emails to ensure seamless mail-client unsubscribe
Email consent and complaint prevention: setting clear expectations and frequency to avoid user frustration
Gmail sender guidelines: mandatory baseline requirements for all senders sending to personal Gmail accounts
Bulk sender requirements: additional mandatory rules for senders delivering 5,000+ daily messages (DMARC, one-click)
Sending-frequency management: avoiding sudden volume spikes that trigger automated spam filters
List hygiene: sunset policies for purging subscribers inactive for 90-180 days
Gmail Postmaster Tools overview: monitoring domain reputation, IP reputation, spam rate, and delivery errors
Deliverability monitoring: utilizing free deliverability testing tools (mail-tester, MXToolbox) in safe sandboxes
Troubleshooting rejected messages: analyzing SMTP error codes (550, 421) and bounce logs
Sender compliance checklist: the pre-flight deliverability checklist every email marketer must verify
